newsitem.title: USA: Central and South West units solicit proxies.
newsitem.headline: Central and South West units solicit proxies.

text.p: Central and South West Corp said its utility subsidiaries were soliciting proxies ahead of special shareholder meetings to consider amending parts of the units' articles of incorporation related to debt restrictions.
The amendment would remove a provision of the articles that limits the subsidiaries' ability to issue unsecured debt, including short-term debt, the company said.

Utility subsidiary Central Power and Light Co would hold its meeting April 7 while Public Service Co of Oklahoma, Southwestern Electric Power Co and West Texas Utilities Co would meet on April 16, the company said.
Central and South West said the debt restrictions limited the units' financial flexibility. The subsidiaries believed they could be at a competitive disadvantage if the restrictions were not removed.

If the proposed amendment is approved and adopted, Public Service Co of Oklahoma, Southwestern Electric and West Texas Utilities would each make a special cash payment of $1.00 per share to preferred shareholders who voted in favor of the proposed amendment, the company said.
If the amendment is approved and adopted, Central Power and Light would make a special cash payment of $0.25 per share, the company said.

Central and South West would offer to purchase all outstanding shares of preferred stock of Public Service Co of Oklahoma, Southwestern Electric and West Texas Utilities and Central Power's 4.20 percent and 4.00 percent cumulative preferred stock. To tender, holders had to vote in favor of the amendment, the company said.
The units would make the payment if those shares were not tendered pursuant to Central and South West's tender offer, the company said.
